activities.title: Follow the stock through time.
activities.objective: Separate stock that is on hand from stock expected before a departure.
steps: Read the departures from earliest to latest. Carry earlier allocations forward instead of starting with a fresh stock count each time.
At each departure, compare the cumulative kits allocated with stock projected to be available by that time.
Identify the first shortage, if any. Investigate the current ETA and the affected commitments before choosing a change.
activities.prompt: Which part of your projection would change if the expected stock arrived after that departure?

activities.title: Check the load as a whole.
activities.objective: Reconcile each order total with the shared space on a departure.
steps: Read across each order: its allocations must add up to the ordered quantity.
Read down each departure: every order on that trip shares the same vehicle capacity.
After changing one cell, check both its order total and its departure load before reviewing the plan again.
activities.prompt: Does your proposed change create a quantity mismatch or move the capacity problem to another trip?

activities.title: Read the promise before changing the plan.
activities.objective: Distinguish a scheduled arrival, a cumulative deadline and a recorded customer agreement.
steps: For each recorded milestone, count only kits on departures that arrive by its deadline.
A later cumulative milestone includes earlier deliveries; do not add its quantity as a second separate order.
Check any no-split condition. If a promise may need to change, ask the relevant customer what is permitted and record a supported agreement before using new terms.
activities.prompt: Which deadline or condition is currently unmet, and what source would authorize a different promise?

activities.title: Count the trips you actually use.
activities.objective: Distinguish a shared departure fee from a fee per order or kit.
steps: Mark each departure that carries at least one kit.
Add its flat fee once, even when several orders share the trip. An empty departure contributes no fee.
Compare that sum with the budget. Any change to reduce cost still needs stock, capacity and promise checks.
activities.prompt: Which fees are included in this review, and what would need rechecking if a departure became unused?

activities.title: Leave a trace someone can follow.
activities.objective: Separate known facts, projections and unresolved work in the handoff.
steps: Identify the reviewed plan and facts it uses, including any customer agreement that was actually recorded.
Keep expected replenishment visible as an assumption. A feasible projection is not proof of receipt or delivery.
Check that unresolved observations remain in the handoff so the next person can see what still needs attention.
activities.prompt: What does this record establish, and what would the next shift still need to confirm?
